b: I made the original post 3 years ago, and I remembered it because my aunt (39f) casually brought up me (27f) being her surrogate again at a small family gathering. My aunt was talking to my mom and me about how if she were to have a baby, she would likely need a surrogate, "like if maybe OP would want to for us someday" and she moved past that comment and was talking about her favorite baby names. Since she didn't directly ask me this time, I just didn't comment on it.

Looking back on the original post, I see how naive and anxious I was. A lot of things have changed since I made the original post. I feel a lot more sure of myself and in my capability to say no, my husband and I are married, I know I want to have a baby, and we've been struggling with infertility for over 2 years. We have "unexplained infertility" on my part, all we know is that my follicles don't mature and I have an ovulation problem. I have done 4 rounds of medication to try to stimulate follicle maturation with no luck, and one round of shots in March of this year to stimulate follicle maturation. The round of shots did allow me to have 3 mature follicles, but that did not result in a pregnancy. We're open to trying shots again in the future, but we have put trying to conceive on pause for now. Our journey to parenthood looks a little different than I had expected it to, and I've spent some time grieving that, but I know everything will be okay. I was always sympathetic towards my aunt's fertility struggles, but I had no idea what it was like to WANT to have a baby like I did when my husband and I started to try to conceive, and that makes me really sad that she has been dealing with this for so long.

I still know I don't want to be a surrogate for anyone, even if/when I am able to have/carry my own baby. I do wonder if it's worth trying to have a conversation with my aunt saying I am not interested in being a surrogate, or just ignore the comments like I have been doing. My aunt did pull me to the side a few years ago asking about it and I said no, but clearly she's still thinking about it. Would it be worth it for me to bring it up and say "please stop mentioning me possibly some day being your surrogate because I don't want to be a surrogate for anyone," or just leave it alone since there hasn't been a formal discussion about it? I imagine there hasn't been a formal discussion about it because I haven't had my own baby, so do I just wait until then or bring it up now/next time she mentions it in passing? I don't know if it would be even worth bringing it up if there isn't a formal discussion about it.
